extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of a lecture series on comparative European literature and dramatic theory
extracted.subtask_description: A compiled list of lecture questions intended to prompt close critical reading and comparative analysis of drama, poetry, prose, and literary history across national traditions (ancient to 18th/19th-century Europe). Useful as a study guide for literary criticism and the production/assessment of poetic and dramatic works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of tragic conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: What tragedies are examples of the first mode? the second? the third? For whom is the third mode of dramatic conclusion best adapted?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish three species/modes of tragic conclusion; classify plays (e.g., Aeschylus, Sophocles, moderns) by mode and assess suitability to audience/genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfection of a kind of tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes the perfection of this kind of tragedy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the formal, thematic, and emotional qualities that realize the 'perfection' of a tragic mode; consider unity, catharsis, moral effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial fondness for a tragic mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Who had a peculiar fondness for this mode?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify a dramatist's consistent preference for a mode and how it shapes their œuvre (e.g., Aeschylus, Sophocles, Shakespeare).

rubrics_metrics.name: Romantic essence and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: In what does the essence of the romantic consist? How might all poetry have some claim to the epithet 'romantic'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define 'romantic' qualities in poetry/drama and evaluate works for those characteristics (imagination, emotion, novelty, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility of romantic with antique
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the romantic inconsistent with the ancient and the true antique? What is said of the romantic in the ancient tragedians?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether 'romantic' elements can coexist with classical forms; cite ancient tragedians as counterexamples or confirmations.

rubrics_metrics.name: National suitability of dramatic forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Why must every nation invent its own form of the drama? Why cannot any modern nation lay down effectual laws for another?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge dramatic forms for cultural/national fit — consider language, social institutions, religion, and national character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of imitation from distant schools
rubrics_metrics.description: By whom should Calderon be studied as a distant specimen of excellence? Why is the external form of the Spanish drama not suitable for Northern Europe?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Calderon (Spanish model) as a comparative case; analyze cross-cultural obstacles (tone, religion, audience expectations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief faults of a dramatist (Calderon example)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the chief fault of Calderon? How would the effect of the denouement be increased?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify structural or stylistic flaws (e.g., diffuse plotting, excessive ornament) and propose remedies to heighten dramatic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shakespeare's faults and general conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: What fault has Shakespeare? What is generally the conclusion of Shakespeare's dramas?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically appraise Shakespeare's weaknesses (e.g., structural looseness) while noting his characteristic endings and moral/political outlooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shakespeare's character and religious/moral position
rubrics_metrics.description: Whom does the author think that Shakespeare resembles more than a Christian? In what does the Christianity of this poet consist?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze the moral/religious sentiments in Shakespeare's works and compare them to prevailing religious identities; be cautious about projecting modern categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of sonnets and lyrics for authorial insight
rubrics_metrics.description: When had Shakespeare recourse to sonnets? What do these sonnets show? For what are his lyrics very important? What do they show to be his character?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lyric and sonnet evidence to infer poet's interior life, aesthetic priorities, and technical range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blending of the fearful and the beautiful
rubrics_metrics.description: With what is the fearful, the horrible, the revolting, blended in his poetry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how disturbing elements are harmonized with beauty; examine tonal balance and aesthetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form excellence in Shakespeare's writings
rubrics_metrics.description: Why is the form of Shakespeare's writings good and excellent?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess formal virtues (characterization, dramatic variety, language) that constitute excellence; consider national reception and translation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautions for national adoption of form
rubrics_metrics.description: Why should not Germans adopt the form or sentiment of his writings as their exclusive model?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warn against uncritical transplantation of another nation's dominant dramatist; emphasize adaptation to national idiom and taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of Spenser and Milton
rubrics_metrics.description: For what are Aeschylus and Sophocles worthy of admiration? What models did Spenser and Milton follow? Towards what is the art of poetry entirely directed in Milton's works?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare influences and aims: measure poets by model choice, didactic aims, and the direction of poetic art (e.g., moral, political, religious).

rubrics_metrics.name: Main defects and remedies in a major poet (Milton)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the main defect of Milton? How did he afterwards seek to remedy this? In what does the excellence of his epic worth consist?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify weaknesses (e.g., obscurity, inequality) and later modifications; evaluate epic excellence by scope, diction, and imaginative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Danger of exclusive standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Has it been advantageous to English poetry that it has followed Milton more than Spenser? Why would any exclusive standard be injurious to the English language?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue for linguistic and stylistic plurality; avoid treating one master as sole model for an entire literary tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language formation and dialectal mixture
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the consequence of a language being formed of two different dialects? Who is the most Teutonic of English poets? Who inclines to the Latin part of the English tongue?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how mixed origins shape poetic vocabulary and style; analyze individual poets' linguistic leanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function and character of allegory (Spenser)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the character of the allegory which is the ground-work of Spenser's chief poem?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess allegorical systems for ethical clarity, narrative coherence, and imaginative richness; consider whether allegory serves interest or burdens it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of lyrical element in tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Why must the imitator of the tragedy of the ancients be as much a lyrical as a dramatic poet? What was the consequence of the lyrical part of the ancient tragedy being omitted in that of France?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate tragedies for inclusion of lyric elements (chorus, lyrical passages) and the effects of their omission on emotional range and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character and defects of French tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: What does the French tragedy express? Why is it not adapted for the model of any other theatre? How is French tragedy most commonly judged?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze French tragedy's rhetorical emphasis, classical derivation, and national specificity; judge adaptability across cultures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Racine and Corneille: character and rank
rubrics_metrics.description: How does Racine rank as a poet? What is said of Corneille? What could be wished in regard to the poetry itself?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare their strengths (style, passion, rhetorical skill) and shortcomings; discuss ideal improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boileau's precepts and their effects
rubrics_metrics.description: What fact proves the injury which Boileau's precepts had on French poetry? What was one of Boileau's great rules of criticism? Did Racine and Corneille adhere to this rule?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider prescriptive critical rules' impact on creativity; weigh conformity versus innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefaces and assertions of Voltaire
rubrics_metrics.description: What assertions are always contained in the prefaces of Voltaire? What have Lessing and others proven to be faults of the French poets?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prefaces as programmatic statements; identify recurring critical positions and their implications on literary practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: French literary language reform and academy
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the first attempt of the French Academy, founded by Richelieu? In what is their success of this attempt shown?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate institutional language/policy interventions and their measurable outcomes on style and national literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: National character in poetry and local influence
rubrics_metrics.description: How does poetry become local? What is the object of poems that treat only of modern society? Are marks of genius ever found in this species of poetry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess works for local color versus universal significance; determine when topicality coexists with lasting genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative merit of translated heroic/tragic works
rubrics_metrics.description: Can a heroic poem or tragedy be well comprehended if translated into a different language?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate translatability of epic/tragic effects—consider idiom, cultural references, and formal constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of national ballads and popular poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: What produced a love for old ballads and popular poems? What fostered the love of ancient national ballads in England?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the role of national memory and oral tradition in forming poetic tastes and revival movements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of prose styles across nations
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the character of the prose of Voltaire? Of Diderot? Of Buffon? Of Rousseau?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorize national prose styles by clarity, elegance, argumentative mode, and moral orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romance/novel function and national adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: What did romance become in the hands of Voltaire, Rousseau, and Diderot? Why did they so often use the romance? Whom did the French imitate in this?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze the functional uses of prose fiction (satire, moral experiment, social critique) and reasons for national schools' adoption of the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation vs originality in national poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Why can an imitation of another nation never be successful? When should the foundations of national character and national poetry be laid?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for rooted originality; assess timing and social conditions required for authentic national poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of materialism/new philosophy on literature
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the influence of materialism on poetry and fancy? What became predominant in the new philosophy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate philosophical currents (materialism, rationalism) for their constraining or enabling effects on imagination, subject-matter, and stylistic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and revival strategies for corrupt languages
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the best means of recalling a language from entire corruption? What two causes prevent the Messiad from becoming a universal favorite?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider translation, original production, patronage, and formal expectations as levers to revive or reform a language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal devices: rhyme vs alliteration and language fit
rubrics_metrics.description: In what languages is alliteration to be found? Why is not rhyme as necessary in the German as in the French language?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match formal poetic devices to phonological and historical properties of languages when composing or assessing verse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical writing: unity of history and philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Why should history and philosophy be united? What is the real importance of the histories of mankind?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess historiography for philosophical depth and moral/human understanding, not merely chronicle or anecdote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for surpassing ancient historians
rubrics_metrics.description: In what respect can we never equal the great historians of antiquity? How can we surpass them? In order to do this what style is the best?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance reverence for ancient models with aims to exceed them through broader materials and a style suited to modern complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: National intellectual recovery and influence of thinkers
rubrics_metrics.description: What caused the modern recovery of intellect/letters after repression? What influence did authors like Bacon, Descartes, Locke, Newton have on literature and philosophy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace intellectual lineage and assess how scientific and philosophical revolutions reshape literary themes, methods, and critical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing the dangers of disguised error
rubrics_metrics.description: Why does error appear to be less dangerous when open and complete than when half-formed and disguised?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically evaluate ideological and philosophical trends for subtle corrosive effects on moral and literary culture; prefer transparency in critique.
